title: Three or four blanks in a retell
statement: How many blanks a fill-in-the-blank retell should have is unsettled, since a component specification and a later procedure document set different counts.
example: One component specification sets exactly four blanks, while a later procedure document sets three core words and never blanks the taught word.
detail: The curriculum's lesson-component specification makes the summary after the read-aloud a compressed, causal retell with exactly four blanks on the links in the child's mental model, with the taught word featuring in it. An updated procedure document sets three core words, verbatim and tapped in order, with the taught word never blanked, and a dated ruling chose it over the named designs, after which a three-word cloze was built into four lessons. Another lesson's instruction blanks the taught word in a closing sentence, an exception to the document the three-word ruling rests on, and the three-or-four question was left to ride with the next branch. Whether the taught word may be one of the blanks is a second open question.
against: A dated ruling chose the three-word form for four lessons (`grade3-reading/_archive/handovers/HANDOVER-2026-09-24.md`, line 264), so for those lessons the count is settled; the taught-word question and the rest of the course are not.
